title: Arctic Azolla event
summary: Around 49 million years ago, at the end of the Early Eocene, the freshwater fern Azolla grew abundantly on the Arctic Ocean surface, as drill cores from the central Arctic show, pointing to a low-salinity surface setting. Researchers suggest burial of its organic matter may have helped lower atmospheric CO2, and the end of the phase coincides with the early shift from hothouse towards icehouse.

uncertainty.note: Range follows the ~49.5-48.5 Myrs phase given by Brinkhuis (Oslo); the 2004 IODP release says only "around 49 million years ago". The atlas id uses 47 Ma. Years are Ma counted back from the present with no 1950 offset.

as_recorded.value: the end of the Early Eocene (~49 Ma)

where.historical_name: Arctic Ocean, Early Eocene; no polities

importance.justification: An Arctic bloom proposed as a carbon sink near the end of the Early Eocene hothouse.
